title: Yunhai French grammar bank
scope: Grammar required for robust NCLC 7 / TEF Canada reading and writing. This is a learnable rule index, not a list of every lexical exception in French.

familiarity_scale.1: Encountered or attempted, but not reliable.
familiarity_scale.2: Demonstrated some independent understanding or use in a familiar context.
familiarity_scale.4: Reliable across different contexts, including producing French.
familiarity_scale.5: Consistently reliable across varied contexts and relevant forms.

rules.rule: Basic declarative order: subject + conjugated verb + complements.
Subject pronouns: je, tu, il/elle/on, nous, vous, ils/elles; use on and nous appropriately.
Present tense of être for identity, state, profession and location.
Present tense of avoir and common expressions with avoir (age, faim, besoin, envie, peur).
Regular -er present endings, including spelling changes such as manger and commencer.
Regular -ir and -re present endings.
Reflexive verbs in the present: me/te/se/nous/vous/se + verb.
High-frequency irregular present forms: aller, faire, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, venir, prendre, mettre, dire, voir, savoir and connaître.
Placement of ordinary adverbs and frequency adverbs in a simple sentence.
Use il y a for existence and c'est / ce sont for identification.
Noun gender; determiner and adjective agreement with masculine and feminine nouns.
Regular plurals and common irregular plural patterns (-al to -aux, -eau to -eaux).
Definite articles le, la, l' and les for specific, general and abstract reference.
Indefinite articles un, une and des for non-specific count nouns.
Partitive articles du, de la, de l' and des; de after negation and quantity expressions where required.
Contractions with à and de: au, à la, à l', aux, du, de la, de l' and des.
Possessive determiners agree with the possessed noun: mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses, etc.
Demonstrative determiners ce, cet, cette and ces; use -ci and -là to distinguish.
Adjective gender and number agreement, including frequent irregular forms.
Usual adjective position and common position changes that alter meaning.
Comparisons and superlatives: plus/moins/aussi ... que; le/la/les plus or moins.
Quantifiers and indefinite determiners: beaucoup de, peu de, assez de, trop de, chaque, plusieurs, quelques, aucun and certain.
Standard negation ne ... pas, including elision before a vowel or mute h.
Extended negation: ne ... jamais, plus, rien, personne, aucun and que.
Questions with intonation, est-ce que and inversion; choose register appropriately.
Question words: qui, que/qu'est-ce que, quoi, où, quand, comment, pourquoi, combien and quel.
Agreement of quel and interrogative lequel forms after prepositions.
Stressed pronouns moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux and elles after prepositions and for emphasis.
Direct-object pronouns le, la, l' and les before the conjugated verb.
Indirect-object pronouns lui and leur for verbs taking à + person.
y for à + thing/place and en for de + thing or a quantity.
Order of two object pronouns before a verb.
Object-pronoun placement with infinitives.
Pronouns with the imperative: affirmative after the verb; negative before it.
Demonstrative pronouns celui, celle, ceux and celles.
Possessive pronouns le mien, la mienne, les miens, etc.
Indefinite, reflexive and reciprocal pronouns.
Passé composé with avoir or être plus past participle.
Main verbs and reflexive verbs that take être in the passé composé.
Past-participle agreement with être and with a preceding direct object where required.
Imparfait for description, background, habitual past action and ongoing state.
Passé composé versus imparfait: completed event versus setting, habit or ongoing action.
Plus-que-parfait for an action completed before another past reference point.
Recent past: venir de + infinitive.
Near future: aller + infinitive.
Futur simple for plans, predictions, promises and formal future reference.
Futur antérieur for completion before a future point and past supposition.
Present conditional for politeness, advice, wishes and hypothetical results.
Past conditional for unreal past results, regret and reported information.
Time and duration: depuis, il y a, pendant, en, pour and dans.
Action in progress: être en train de + infinitive.
Use an infinitive after a conjugated modal or preference verb where French requires it.
Common verb patterns: à + infinitive, de + infinitive, or bare infinitive.
Imperative forms, including irregular forms and negative imperative.
Causation or services: faire + infinitive.
Permission and perception: laisser + infinitive; voir/entendre + infinitive.
Present participle and gérondif (en + present participle) for simultaneous action, method, cause or contrast.
Passive voice: être + past participle, agreement and par/de agent phrases.
Impersonal forms: il faut, il semble, il paraît, il est possible/important de and il y a.
Use general on or pronominal passive when more natural than an explicit passive.
Coordinating conjunctions: et, mais, ou, donc, or, ni and car.
Cause: parce que, puisque, comme, car and grâce à.
Result and explanation: donc, alors, ainsi, par conséquent, c'est pourquoi and en effet.
Contrast and concession: mais, pourtant, cependant, toutefois, tandis que, malgré and bien que.
Purpose: pour + infinitive, afin de + infinitive, pour que and afin que.
Time clauses: quand, lorsque, dès que, pendant que, avant que, après que, jusqu'à ce que and depuis que.
Relative pronouns qui, que, dont and où; choose the pronoun from its grammatical role.
Relative lequel forms, including auquel and duquel, after prepositions.
Ce qui, ce que, ce dont and ce à quoi for an entire idea or unspecified thing.
Indirect questions and reported speech, including tense and pronoun changes after a past reporting verb.
Punctuation and sentence boundaries that avoid run-on sentences in formal writing.
Present subjunctive formation, including common irregular stems.
Subjunctive after necessity, desire, emotion, doubt, possibility and judgment.
Indicative versus subjunctive after common conjunctions, including bien que, pour que, avant que, à condition que and après que.
Subjunctive in relative clauses with uncertain, desired, superlative or evaluated antecedents.
Real condition: si + present with future, imperative or present result.
Hypothetical present/future: si + imparfait with present conditional.
Unreal past: si + plus-que-parfait with past conditional.
Do not use future or conditional directly after si in standard conditional clauses.

categories.name: Prepositions, register and TEF writing control

rules.rule: Location prepositions: à, dans, en, au, aux, chez, sur, sous, devant, derrière, entre and parmi.
Geographic prepositions with countries, regions and cities.
Tu versus vous and polite requests with conditional or imperative forms.
Formal written openings, closings and address forms without register mixing.
Consistent agreement across determiners, nouns, adjectives, past participles and pronouns.
Paragraph grammar: claim, reason, example and conclusion linked with varied connectors.
Opinion, qualification and hedging with appropriate indicative, subjunctive and conditional structures.
Nominalization and impersonal structures for concise formal writing.
Proofread for agreement, tense consistency, pronoun reference, articles, prepositions and negation.
